Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to performance qualification for the Private/VPC deployment:

- Target SLOs we heard from the call:
  - 99th percentile latency target: 200ms for short prompt generation (~256 tokens)
  - Sustained throughput: 50 concurrent requests, average attn length 512 tokens
  - Streaming/partial-response requirement for chat UI (server-side chunking ok)

- Network and infra items we need from ACME to validate throughput:
  1) Typical egress path (VPN/peering) and expected RTT from ACME app servers to the VPC where Redwood will run (or your on-prem proxy).
  2) Any enforced egress NAT or proxy that may add 10-100ms of headroom.
  3) Expected sustained connections and TLS session reuse policies for long-lived sockets.

Action items / timeline:
- ACME to share network diagram + baseline RTTs (Alicia / Infra) — ideally by EOD Wed 5/13.
- Aditya to draft performance test plan (load profile, concurrency shape, streaming checks) — ETA 5/14.

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from infra: 

- We currently peer to AWS via a dedicated Direct Connect circuit for most traffic; expected RTT to your planned region (us-west-2) is ~8-12ms from our app cluster. We also have an Azure region for DR with ~25ms.
- We terminate TLS on an internal ALB; there is a NAT gateway for egress, but we can open a peering/VPC attachment if needed.
- We typically reuse TLS sessions for backend RPCs, but client browsers do not keep connections; the app server will maintain long-lived connections to the inference endpoint.

1) For streaming responses, do you recommend server-initiated chunking or HTTP/2 server-push? What do you validate in performance tests as the streaming SLO?
2) If we run Redwood Private on our VPC, what additional network headroom should we plan for to meet the 200ms p99 target?

Hi Alicia — quick answers and what we'll validate in the perf run: 

1) Streaming: we support chunked transfer over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 streaming. For the tests we recommend using HTTP/2 with multiplexed streams from the app server to the inference endpoint; that most closely mirrors production browser behavior and keeps connection overhead low. For server-side chunking we validate per-chunk latency (time-to-first-chunk) and sustained chunk rate so your UI can render progressively.

2) Network headroom: plan for an additional 25-40ms of internal network processing budget to account for TLS termination, ALB/NAT traversal, and any proxying. That means to reliably hit 200ms p99 for a 256-token gen you'll want app->inference RTT ideally <= 60-80ms (includes our server processing). Since you quoted ~8-12ms to us-west-2 over Direct Connect, that's a good starting point.

What we'll validate in the performance test:
- Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and time-to-first-chunk under streaming workloads.
- P99 and P50 latency at 50 concurrent requests with a steady-state workload (token length distribution you provided).
- Throughput saturation curve and graceful degradation: how latency changes at 50, 100, 200 concurrent requests.
- Connection reuse and TLS handshake impact: we'll run with both long-lived connections and frequent reconnects to quantify differences.

Request: can you share typical payload sizes, and any expected spikes (e.g., batch jobs that could create sudden burst traffic)? Also please confirm whether your peering is active to us-west-2 or if direct-connect terminates in a different AZ — that affects egress path.

I'll attach the perf test plan draft (we'll share a doc link after internal review).

—Aditya
